lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For a thousand years, geniuses thought your eyes shoot lasers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then Cairo polymath Ibn al-Haytham stepped into total darkness.

lines.speaker: alhazen
lines.text: If eyes shoot light, why can't you see now?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Through one tiny pinhole, candle rays raced straight, crossed over, and projected the flame...

lines.speaker: alhazen
lines.text: Because light enters your eye—it never shoots out!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He built the Camera Obscura—and unlocked human vision.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every phone camera today? Still inside his dark room.
